correctness.rationale: Explicit rational convex mixtures are verified for each cyclic chord class. For each candidate, the residual inner product with every active cycle edge equals the maximum over all cycle edges, exactly satisfying the variational projection criterion. Squared residual norms are 0, 1, 5/6 or 3/4 as claimed. Strict convexity of squared norm across distinct farthest residuals proves that no nonvertex point reaches the Hausdorff maximum. Exact rational checker reproduces 10,659 cases in orders 3 through 40 and independent constrained numerical QPs check 219 cases to order 11. Infinite conclusion follows from the uniform case proof, not finite trials.

value.rationale: The cycle edge polytope is the canonical Hamiltonian-cycle sparsification of the rank-two uniform edge polytope, retaining a vanishing fraction of its vertices. Computing the complete ambient Euclidean projection spectrum of all omitted chords, the exact Hausdorff saturation at squared radius 5/6, the exceptional 4-cycle radius 1, and the whole continuous farthest-point locus provides a natural nontrivial geometric approximation invariant. A strict 1/12 next-vertex-shell gap in all orders at least six identifies which omissions dominate approximation error. This precise metric invariant is useful as a sharp graph-edge sparsification benchmark rather than a contrived finite slice.
